_meta.purpose: Publishable rule-change events for the public changes feed.
_meta.generated_from: worker/src/mobility_rules.json (batch research) + automated day-to-day source monitoring. AuditLab value-spotcheck note (2026-08-21): this line says '4 currently promoted' under a FOUND reading (DC was DiffLab find #4), but `live_monitoring_count` below says 3 under a SOURCE reading (events where source == "difflab_reg_change_engine": Missouri x2 + Idaho) -- DC's event was hand-rewritten from the primary source on 08-14, so its `source` field no longer matches the engine. 3 is authoritative and is what actually renders live; `coverage_stats.real_events_found` uses the same SOURCE reading. Do NOT bump `live_monitoring_count` to 4 to make these agree -- that would be a live overclaim on /rule-changes/. This line's own wording is the thing that's imprecise, not the count below it.
_meta.separable: Deliberately independent of the mobility determination engine (AuditLab MON-2, 2026-08-06: the engine shipped to production 2026-07-30 -- /firm/mobility/check, /firm/mobility/check-batch, /firm/mobility/coverage, and the /firm-mobility/ Practice Privilege Check UI are all live; this note previously said HELD, which stopped being true and would have misled a future maintainer about what's deployed). This feed publishes change facts + citations only and stays architecturally independent of that engine either way -- a change fact does not require or imply a mobility determination for the same state.
_meta.status_derivation: Structured fields ONLY (rule_changes_on presence + direction, or the monitoring pipeline's own classified status). Status is NOT inferred from prose: 27 of 55 mobility records match enacted/proposed/rule signals simultaneously, so a regex label would be a guess. Records whose status cannot be established from structure are not emitted.
_meta.reverification_rule: needs_reverification=true means the effective date has passed and we have NOT re-checked. The page must say 'effective [date]; we re-verify on/after that date' -- never 'is now in effect'.

events.summary_public: A new enactment of the CPA firm permit issuance-and-renewal statute takes effect, replacing the version in effect since 2020. The board may grant or renew permits to practice as a certified public accounting firm to applicants meeting the qualifications in this chapter.
events.status_evidence: Effective - 28 Aug 2026, 6 histories ... 326.289 8/28/2026 [Effective, no End date] ... The board may grant or renew permits to practice as a certified public accounting firm to applicants that demonstrate their qualifications in accordance with this chapter.

events.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. section 326.283
events.summary_public: A new enactment of the individual out-of-state CPA reciprocity/practice-privilege statute takes effect, replacing the version in effect since 2017. Under the new version, an individual with a valid, unrestricted CPA license from any state may practice in Missouri without obtaining a Missouri license, notifying the board, or paying a fee, provided the individual met qualifying education/experience requirements at initial licensure (or held qualifying practice privileges as of 2024-12-31 under a grandfather provision).
events.status_evidence: Effective - 28 Aug 2026, 5 histories ... 326.283 8/28/2026 [Effective, no End date] ... An individual whose principal place of business, domicile, or residency is not in this state and who holds a valid and unrestricted license in good standing to practice public accounting from any state shall have all the privileges of licensees of this state without the need to obtain a license

events.summary_public: Indiana's CPA mobility rule has been state-level substantial-equivalence mobility (based on the practitioner's home state's overall status) since 2007 -- that part is not changing. What's pending for 2027 is a shift in Indiana's own licensure pathways, which the Board has begun overlaying onto mobility and reciprocity through a non-binding policy document; by the Board's own statement, if that document conflicts with the actual statute or rules, the statute and rules control today. See our full Indiana guide and the citation below for the details.

events.citation: S.2946, An Act relative to modernizing the pathway to becoming a certified public accountant (194th Mass. General Court), Section 5 (amending M.G.L. c. 112, section 87B(h)(2)) and Section 6 (effective date)
events.summary_public: A bill (S.2946) that would move Massachusetts's CPA mobility rule to individual-criteria mobility (based on the practitioner's own license and experience, not their home state's status) passed the Senate 37-0 on 2026-02-12 but has not been enacted -- it has sat in the House Ways and Means committee since 2026-02-17 with no further action. If it passes as written, it takes effect January 1, 2027, with a grandfather clause for anyone who already holds a valid out-of-state CPA certificate as of December 31, 2025. Outcome is not yet settled.
events.status_evidence: Bill history (malegislature.gov/Bills/194/S2946): 2026-02-05 reported from Senate Ways and Means; 2026-02-12 passed to be engrossed, Roll Call #133, Yeas 37 Nays 0; 2026-02-17 read and referred to House Ways and Means. No action logged since. Bill text, Section 5: strikes the NASBA-verified substantial-equivalence test from 87B(h)(2) and replaces it with 'the person has met the educational and experience requirements listed in subsection (e) of section 87A1/2 and has passed the Uniform Certified Public Accountant Examination' -- individual-criteria, with a grandfather proviso for anyone holding a valid out-of-state certificate on or before 2025-12-31. Section 6: 'This act shall take effect on January 1, 2027.'

events.summary_public: Our two primary sources for District of Columbia disagree about parts of its mobility rule. The individual practice-privilege section we cite here was amended by emergency legislation effective 2026-08-10 -- that amendment has now been captured from the D.C. Council's own bulk-download channel (see the separate rule-change entry for D.C. Act 26-399) but remains single-source pending re-verification. A separate, still-unresolved conflict remains on the firm side: the statute exempts most no-office out-of-state firms from registering for non-attest work, while older compiled regulations still on the books read as requiring a permit of every nonresident firm. We record the stricter reading and withhold a determination rather than guess.

events.citation: IDAPA 24.30.01 (Idaho Accountancy Rules), Docket No. 24-3001-2601
events.summary_public: A proposed rulemaking would: (1) create a new pathway to licensure for candidates and make minor adjustments to accommodate statutory changes in line with HB 563 from 2026; (2) transition renewal dates from a fixed June 30 date to birthdate-based renewals with an expanded window to accommodate peak tax season; and (3) remove outdated rule language. Outcome is not yet settled -- a public hearing is scheduled, not yet adopted.
events.status_evidence: NOTICE OF RULEMAKING -- PROPOSED RULE ... This contemplated rulemaking: (1) facilitates a new pathway to licensure for candidates and makes minor adjustments to accommodate for statutory changes in line with HB 563 from 2026; (2) transitions from June 30 to birthdate-based renewals with an expanded window to accommodate peak tax season; and (3) removes outdated language.

events.citation: D.C. Act 26-399 (Business Licensing Reform and Accountancy Practice Emergency Amendment Act of 2026), section 3(b)(3), amending D.C. Official Code section 47-2853.49
events.summary_public: D.C. replaced its NASBA substantial-equivalency mobility test with individual criteria (a valid, unrestricted CPA license in good standing from any state, plus exam, education, and experience requirements met at initial licensure), effective August 10, 2026, with a savings clause preserving privileges held before that date; we re-verify on or after the effective date before treating the change as settled. Important: this is EMERGENCY legislation that expires November 8, 2026 by its own terms -- a permanent version (Bill 26-494) passed the Council but must complete congressional review, so the rule's status should be re-checked around that expiry date.
events.status_evidence: Captured from the D.C. Council's own bulk-download channel (DCCouncil/law-xml-codified publication branches, confirmed word-for-word identical to the live D.C. Law Library text including the emergency-amendment expiry note); promoted from automated source monitoring (DiffLab event #4, 2026-08-14).
